purpose: Use the existing single-security QFQ full-prefix inputs and cached brick series to calculate the repaired rebuild observation and explicitly named brick source fields.
owner: existing V4 A-share daily producer; no new producer or scheduler

rebuild.status: LOCAL_RULE_DERIVED_FROM_CORRECTED_SOURCE; local module and contract have their own separate SHA identities
rebuild.repair: Use full prefix MA14/28/57/114 for current yellow and prefix slices ending 4 and 9 bars before current for the two historical yellow values; require 124 observations before returning a boolean.
rebuild.warmup: kb_rebuild=null, reason=INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY, required=124 and available=observed prefix count when fewer than 124 bars exist. Invalid required inputs have their own reason, not a history-shortage reason.
rebuild.source_semantics: Retain the corrected source's first matching up-volume day among the latest 15 observations, its partial initial volume slice divided by 5, strict comparisons, and positive-yellow guard. The implementation does not itself require a golden-cross event even though its prose mentions one; this local value is a source-implementation research signal, not full original-rule certification.
rebuild.input: close, positive volume, percent change: same stock, ascending unique dates, same bound QFQ generation; caller validates upstream data/calendar/price basis and supplies only the intended as-of index.

brick.input: The existing kb_signal_authority._brick_series full-prefix cached sequence (Python round to two decimals), bound to security/generation/valid HLC prefix and recursive seed. The caller must explicitly affirm validity, seed binding and series_id=KB_AUTHORITY_BRICK_SERIES_B195_V1.
brick.trend: RED when today's source brick value >= yesterday's; otherwise GREEN. Two actual mature values require at least 13 bars. This is a color, not kb_brick_trend_up's separate slope condition.
brick.count: Consecutive source-color run after an observed reversal; if the run starts within synthetic source warmup, value is null with BRICK_RUN_ORIGIN_IN_WARMUP, even if a lower bound is known. Do not label this data gap as a source-rule conflict.
brick.description_patch: On red-to-green the source text interpolates the current green run count in place of the preceding red run. The local rule computes the actual prior red-run count; if its origin is in warmup, the description is null with PREVIOUS_RED_RUN_ORIGIN_IN_WARMUP. Other descriptions retain the source text.
brick.display: These are source pattern descriptions only; never trade instructions or changed buy gates.

incremental: On initial missing-field bootstrap compute only the bound affected stock rows. Persist null reason, required/available history and rule identity. Subsequently compute new dates, newly matured rows after earlier input is actually restored, and rows whose dependent inputs were revised; reuse other validated rows when input/calendar/price basis/rule hashes match. Do not rescan all history solely due to a new generation or export.
acceptance: Candidate source tests and two-stock historical evidence do not imply integration, deployment, API/UI visibility, natural execution, historical PIT or strategy validity.
